caption:
Window seat: still disputed. Some arguments survive every Bhaubeej.

The Droplet Open Cuff is a slim polished open cuff with a round ball on one end and a smooth teardrop on the other, sitting across a small gap. Neither crosses. 18k gold tone plated or rhodium plated, ₹1,599.

Send this to the brother who still takes the window seat. Bhaubeej is next week; consider it a hint. One in each metal works too. Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off. The bag applies BUY2 or BUY3 for you.

[ droplet open cuff · gold tone or rhodium · he can sit in the back ]
first_comment: Tag the sibling who still takes the window seat. Every piece arrives in our blush box · free insured shipping · COD available #NairaFlore #Bhaubeej #BhaiDooj #DemiFineJewellery #NairaPetite
alt_text: Short video. An illustrated blush pink Art Deco building at dusk fills the screen, its three shops lit at street level and every window above dark, a paper lantern beside each. The sky turns to a Diwali night and a lantern lights on the first floor, at the right-hand window, and the view moves in to it: sage green louvred shutters, shut, with a pink paper lantern hanging beside them. The shutters swing open onto a dim, blue-grey night room, where a bracelet shows only as its own cream outline drawing itself, both ends at once, on a striped window-seat cushion. A lamp comes on at the left with a warm apricot glow, the lilac room and the sage and ivory stripes light up, and the outline becomes the real photograph: a slim gold-tone open cuff ending in a round ball on one side and a teardrop on the other, lying across the cushion with a small gap between the two ends. A soft light slides over the gold from the ball to the teardrop. On the wall: WINDOW SEAT: STILL DISPUTED. and 'two ends. one small gap.' A dashed chalk line then runs down the cushion's middle seam, straight through the gap between the ball and the teardrop, stopping short of the metal where the cuff's band lies across it, and the last line appears: 'nobody crosses it.' A brass plate below reads FLAT 103 with the Naira wordmark. The view pulls back to the whole building, now with four windows lit, then a closing card: Flat 103, first floor. Droplet Open Cuff, 18k gold tone plated or rhodium plated. ₹1,599. nairaflore.com. Two endings, one round, one falling. Every piece arrives in our blush box, free insured shipping, COD available.
sound: In-app instrumental (Instagram audio library, no vocals, no lyrics): a light, affectionate santoor piece (search 'santoor', 'indian instrumental calm'), entering at 0.6 s under the ambience, ducked 4 dB under the foley. BAKED into reel.mp4 (synthesised, _build/sfx.py, peak -12.8 dBFS at the bell): 0.0-1.2 s building ambience (street hum, a far scooter passing right to left, a few evening birds; the bed stays on low and rises again over the last 0.5 s so the loop meets itself); 0.20 s the lift-bell, one soft brass ding (B5, ~1.2 s decay) as FLAT 103's kandil lights; 2.20 s a soft wooden hinge, the two louvred leaves creaking open (stick-slip pulses following the leaves' swing, panned apart, the right a hair behind); 3.38 / 3.42 s the leaves touching the wall, two soft wooden knocks, left then right; 4.80 s a small ting with the first sparkle; 6.00-7.15 s a dry, muffled chalk scratch, one stroke for each dash as the line runs down the seam, silent while it hops the cuff; 11.40 s one low chime (E4-B4-E5) as the end card comes in, its tail faded over the last 0.5 s into the loop.
deviations: FINAL REVIEW, item 1 (OUTLINE REMNANT, a white halo on the developed cuff): applied as given. (a) reel.html room(): retract = cl((ms - T.retS) / T.retD), LINEAR (was E.inout), T.retS 3800 and T.retD 700 as the brief has them. (b) room() also returns olOp = 1 - E.sine(cl((ms - T.retS) / T.olD)), T.olD 250 (new), and world/bays/p04.js apply() sets the p-outline layer's opacity from it (S.olOp, default 1 in D, so CLOSED is unchanged; LIT and the cover, retract 1, draw no line either way). The line now fades 3.80 -> 4.05 s while it retracts: at 4.0 s (f120) it is 71 % long at 9.5 % opacity, and from f122 (4.067 s) it is gone. Develop and outline overlap 3.60-4.05 s (0.45 s; the brief asks >= 0.4 s). Mirrored in OPENING(t), because the post's own state sheet shows the outline at .62 and .80 (at .80 it was the same full-strength remnant on the developed cuff): olOp = 1 - sine((t - .66) / .08), so the line fades over t .66-.74, the reel's 0.25 s at OPENING's 0.9 s develop = .30 t. The shared camera test reel/p04-camera-test.html drives OPENING(t) and will show the same on its next render; its mp4 belongs to the world lead and was not re-rendered here.

FINAL REVIEW, item 1, a SECOND CAUSE found by the acceptance test (the develop's scale): with (a) and (b) alone the line was gone from f122, but the cuff's edge ring still differed from the photograph at rest by up to 76-91 levels through f129 (3,472-4,551 ring pixels over 8), and the whole cut-out snapped sharp in one frame at f130 (4.33 s). Cause, isolated with _build/rasterprobe.cjs: the develop's scale was a CSS transform on the img (scale(1.035 - .035 dev), to 4 decimals), and under ANY non-identity transform Chrome draws the cut-out through a softer resampling path. The blur (0.2 px at f122) renders identically to none, and opacity .967 with transform none is 7 levels off rest at most, but scale(1.0001) on the photograph at rest is up to 90 levels off. So the photograph developed into a slightly soft copy of itself and jumped to the true raster only when the scale string reached 1.0000. Changed in p04.js apply(): the same scale (1.035 -> 1 about the centre, the brief's develop) is now the img's own box grown about its centre (left / top / width / height) with transform none throughout, so the image takes the rest path all the way and lands on it continuously. At dev 1 the kit's own box strings go back, so LIT, the cover and every neighbour state draw exactly as before: cover.html re-rendered to a scratch file is 0 pixels off the shipped cover@2x.png, and the shipped cover files were not touched. Opacity 0 -> 1, blur 6 -> 0 px, 0.9 s on the reveal curve: unchanged.

FINAL RENDER (27 Oct 2026, on the final shared world: world.js 21:32, kit/kandil.js 23:09 UTC 26 Oct, the neighbours' bays as they stand): every file re-rendered from its HTML source with the post's own build (reel.html through _build/reelsafe.cjs, no page error at load or in any of the 450 frames; cover.html through tools/render.cjs, no missing image, every font loaded). trace_outline.py, chalk.py, glintmask.py and sfx.py re-run and byte-identical to the shipped assets (md5 of chalk.png, glint-mask.png, sfx.wav unchanged; p04.js's OUTLINE unchanged), so only the world moved. No P4 file needed a fix: p04.js and reel.html are as fix pass 3 left them. (Superseded for the outline and the develop by FINAL REVIEW, item 1: reel.html and p04.js changed after this render.)

FINAL RENDER, the neighbour veil (frame-space sweep): on the shipped reel.mp4 the front is on screen in frames 42-54 of the find (1.40-1.80 s, 13 frames: the find is 1.6 s here, not the camera tests' 1.8 s) and 292-306 of the pull-back (9.73-10.20 s, 15 frames), crossing FLAT 203 upward and SHOP 1 downward from the shared edges (_build/veilinfo.cjs: NVW.coverInfo per frame, fronts mapped to screen by the camera's own matrix). Viewed frame by frame (strip-veil-find.jpg, strip-veil-pull.jpg) and at 1:1 on f44, 47, 50, 53, 296, 300, 304 (_work/fin/veil-fronts.jpg): on SHOP 1 the lac rail cuts the fascia's wordmark from its top and leaves a plastered recess, the shutter and the kandil ahead of it untouched; on FLAT 203 the plate is cut from below and the front climbs the plaster just under the dark window, which leaves the frame as the camera closes; no grey or khaki row at either front, no pop, and the find ends on the still cover's plaster bands exactly (f55 on). The pull-back folds the quiet back into FLAT 103 the same way.

FINAL RENDER, the week-2 sky: frame 0 is week 1's dusk and the sky clock ticks to the Diwali night over 0.2-1.0 s; on the building hold (11.1-11.4 s) the night carries the apricot glow rising from the horizon (rose above it, never grey), the terrace poles stand inside their tiles (P12 its right pole only) with the far wire's spans between them (_work/fin/estab-pair.jpg, frame 0 beside 11.2 s).

FINAL RENDER, the kandil: it reads lit at every scale. At establishing scale FLAT 103's lantern lifts against frame 0's unlit one (warm paper, bright window, core glow); at cover scale the window is the brightest thing on it. Its light is soft on every ground: the hard arc the last pass left across the left leaf's louvres at cover y ~620 is gone (_work/fin/kandil-cmp.jpg, previous cover beside this one). On the shut louvres (2.2 s) the pool runs warm beside the body and passes through a soft olive-grey ring into the sage, the world's documented limit for P4's bluish shut-louvre tone #4A6656 (README C-KANDIL: its nearest colour at hue <= 80 is 8.94 dE away); left as the world set it, nothing in P4 draws over the kandil's light. The lamp pool and the words are untouched by it (below).

LIVE PRICE AND STOCK: re-read from research/roster.json for this render (droplet-open-cuff: price 1599.0, no compare-at, Gold 10 available ₹1,599, Silver 10 available ₹1,599); the end card's '₹1,599' and the caption's figure match. (Last read live from Shopify 26 Oct 06:21 UTC, the same figures.) The brief's guard still applies: re-read the evening of 2 Nov; if Gold is below 8 and Silver is not, swap the cut-out to droplet-open-cuff/01-trim.png (same words); if both are at 5 or fewer, swap to the Pear Point Open Cuff and change the end card. A price change touches only reel.html's end card (price:) and the caption's figure; re-render with sources.rebuild.

COVER EXPORT: cover.jpg is the 1080x1920 reel cover (export.py from cover@2x.png). The grid tile is cover y 240-1680, cropped from cover@2x.png (y 480-3360 -> cover-grid@2x.png) and run through export.py, which writes cover-grid.jpg (1080x1440), cover-grid-45.jpg (1080x1350, the 4:5 centre crop: the kandil's cap and the whole plate stay in) and cover-grid-thumb.png (391x521). cover-thumb.png is that grid thumb (the tile as it shows in the grid on a phone), so export.py's own 9:16 thumb of cover.jpg is overwritten; there is no cover-45.jpg (a 9:16 cover has no 4:5 crop of its own; the 4:5 is the grid tile's).

FIX PASS 3, item 1 (LAMP POP): applied as given. apply() holds the p-light container at opacity 1 right after h.set() and drives the two lamp layers' own opacity with g (lampOv, the overlay; lampSc, the screen): blend mode and opacity on the same element mix the blended result with the room linearly, so there is no isolated group and no plain marigold. Measured on the encoded reel, 3.40-4.30 s (_build/lightscan.py, frames from _build/mp4frames.sh): the lamp region (cover x 160-330, y 640-1000) moves smoothly from the dark room to the lit one with no wash and no snap: the step at 4.17-4.20 s (24 levels) is gone, every frame from 4.03 s moves it by 1.1 levels or less (the kandil's tails sway through it) and the whole frame by 0.19 or less. The pool under the turn (y 800-1000, where the light is) goes from the dark lilac (hue 264) through low-saturation mauve (S <= 16, 3.43-3.60 s) into the warm and then holds 9.9-20.0 deg from 3.67 s to 4.30 s and after, never above 20.1 deg and never above S 34: no marigold excursion. The 4.30 s pool matches the cover (mean difference 1.44 levels, encoded reel vs cover.jpg; 0.62 frame-for-frame before encoding); the 9.2 s frame (words in, lamp at rest) matches the cover across the room at 2.6 levels (H.264 against JPEG, and the kandil's phase). Two of the director's acceptance figures are not met literally, and why: (1) the whole region's mean hue rests at 6.0, not 8-20, because its upper third (y 640-780, beside the turn) is the turn's mauve-lilac ground (hue ~330, S 15), which item 3 asked to keep as it is, and the pool below is now hue 20; (2) inside the lamp region the per-frame change peaks at 9.9 levels (3.53 s) and falls smoothly frame by frame, because the region rises by about 85 levels in the house's 0.9 s lights-on: even a linear ramp would move it 3.1 levels a frame. The whole frame, the item 2 test, stays under 3 (below). Note for the world lead: builders.js lights(g) fades r.light itself, so ANY bay whose r.light container holds a child with a mix-blend-mode paints that child as plain colour until g reaches 1 and then snaps (p02, p03, p07, p08 and p09 also return a p-light container; worth a check). Fixed here inside p04.js only, through the documented API.

FIX PASS 3, item 2 (LIGHTS-ON STEP): h.dark.night.style.opacity = .55 * (1 - g), so the cool veil leaves over the whole lamp-up with h.dark.el (the director's first option; the sine over linear lamp time was not needed). Measured at 270 x 480 on the encoded reel, 3.40-4.30 s: the largest whole-frame mean difference is 2.93 levels (3.53 s; was 5.67 at 3.433 s) and the largest share of pixels moving more than 20 levels is 0.3 % (was 12.6 %); frame by frame 2.40, 2.74, 2.71, 2.93, 2.49, 2.24, 1.95, 1.65, 1.40 ... 0.10, a 0.9 s lights-on with its weight up front, as the reveal curve has it. The dark room at 3.2 s is unchanged: back wall #221A30, cushion #403742 / #38313E, face #332B36, the outline 10.0-11.9 : 1 (_build/darkcheck.py), the same as fix pass 2; the only pixels that differ at 3.2 s are round the kandil, from the shared halo change (kit/kandil.js 14:46 UTC).

FIX PASS 3, item 3 (LAMP RESTING COLOUR): the suggested route (#FFCDA4 .68 at room (30, 620), 280 x 180) was the start; measured, it DARKENED the pool under the turn (L 54 -> 46: the smaller ellipse, centred 120 px lower, left most of cover y 800-1000 in its fringe), so it was tuned on from there (16 variants, _build/lampsweep.cjs through a window.P04_LAMP hook): overlay #F0A028 (yellower, so the pool saturates less) at .80 / .64 at .34 / .12 at .64, centre unchanged (60, 560), 470 x 380; screen #FFD5B4 held flat across its middle (.62 centre, .36 at .6 of its radius), room (30, 560), 340 x 230. Measured on the cover (_build/lampcheck3.py): under the turn (cover x 160-330, y 800-1000, the wall by the cushion's own silhouette) #BD917A, hue 20.1, S 33.9, L 61.1 (lampcheck2's colour test on the same band: #B58874, hue 18.3, S 30.4, L 58.2; both in the target of hue 18-24, S 30-38, L 58-63); its lowest band (y 880-1000) S 38.2, under 40; above y 780 'two ends.' 6.41 : 1 and 'nobody crosses it.' 6.50 : 1 on their ground (6.18 / 6.25 : 1 on its lightest tenth; the ground #553F63 / #533E64, as before); the right wall #45355A. In the 391 x 521 tile the left of the room now reads as a soft apricot pool of lamplight beside the seat rather than a brown smudge. Measured with the shared kandil-halo fix in (it landed at 14:46 UTC: the pool masked to sage, a soft overlay + screen glow on every other ground); that glow lies above y 700 at the left and does not reach the pool. MEASURING NOTE: lampcheck2's wall test (not sage, relative luminance < .35) also drops the lamp's own lightest wall pixels once the pool passes about L 60 (it keeps 18,364 of the band's 30,083 wall pixels), so it reads the pool low; _build/lampcheck3.py masks the wall by the cushion's own silhouette (AI-10's alpha at its placed box) and reports both. The pool was tuned so that BOTH land in the target. Cover, cover-grid and cover-thumb re-exported.

FIX PASS 3, item 4 (PUNCHLINE HOLD): applied as given. T.words[3] 7200 -> 7050, T.pullS 9000 -> 9300, T.endS 11200 -> 11400, T.reset 11900 -> 12000; T.wrap 14000 and the 14.5-15.0 s dissolve unchanged; the chime in _build/sfx.py moved 11.20 -> 11.40 s (now 3.6 s long to the loop's seam, its last 0.5 s faded so its tail, about -45 dBFS there, ends rather than cuts). FIX PASS 3, item 5 (CAPTION): paragraph 2 now reads '18k gold tone plated or rhodium plated, ₹1,599.', the claims rule's exact phrase, as on the end card and in the alt text.

FIX PASS 3, housekeeping: cover.html carried a stray, duplicated comment opener (a P1 line and a second <script> inside the script) from an earlier copy; removed (harmless to the render, but it read as broken). Reels rendered with _build/reelsafe.cjs, a copy of tools/reel.cjs with the same encode settings that aborts on any page error: one probe in this pass caught a shared file mid-edit ('cap is not defined', from another bay) and rendered a broken world, so a render now refuses to finish on one.

FIX PASS 2, item 1 (GLINT): applied as given (backgroundPosition (82.5 - 65 * glint)%, peak .42, shoulders .30, mix-blend-mode screen, glintS 4500 / glintD 1100 / E.inout, sparkles 4.8 / 5.2 s), plus two changes the measurement required. (a) The glint now lives in the room's interior beside the cut-out instead of the close-up layer above it: that layer is a transformed interior, an isolated group, so screen there only blended onto its own empty group. (b) Screen with a near-white band lifts a dark pixel exactly as much as normal paint does (d + a(1 - d) either way), so with the director's numbers alone the drop's dark pixels still fell from 10.0 % to 2.4 % and the ball's to 2.9 %, and the ball and the drop each turned pale cream for 2-3 frames (_work/g/new-sheet.png before the mask). The band is therefore masked by the photograph's own highlights (alpha x smoothstep(.36, .78, luma), _build/glintmask.py -> assets/glint-mask.png): the light brightens what already catches it and the mirror darks keep their shape. Also: with the in-out ease the band crosses EACH END in about 0.2 s (6-7 frames, it is fastest mid-move where the ends sit); it is on the metal 4.73-5.30 s (17 frames) in all, not the ~0.9 s the director estimated for a linear move.

FIX PASS 2, item 2 (DARK ROOM): the two layers are driven separately as asked (night veil .55 * (1 - sine(g / .25)), held at full until the lamp comes up), but the warm multiply eases to .30, not .70, and a cool night multiply (#9CA8D0, p-moon, in the room's own interior under the facade's darkness pair) rises with the leaves and leaves with the lamp. Measured with the director's .70: the cushion was still rose (hue 339-351, S 16-17 %) and the wall L 12.4 %, because #55261E multiplied at .70 reddens the ivory stripes before the veil goes on; even with no warm layer at all a normal #241B2E veil leaves the cushion mauve (hue 309-339). Both layers follow sine(m / .5), so the room is grey-violet by the time the gap shows it (2.8 s; at 2.65 s linear it was hue 336, S 17 %). CLOSED (m 0) and LIT are the world's exactly.

FIX PASS 2, item 3 (TIMING): T.words [4800, 4900, 5400, 7200] exactly as given. 'nobody crosses it.' rises 7.2-7.8 s and is held 1.2 s before the pull-back (still legible at 9.5 s), so it is held less than the house 2.0 s for headlines before the camera moves: the director's call, kept. (SUPERSEDED by fix pass 3, item 4: it now rises at 7.05 s and is held 1.65 s still.)

FIX PASS 2, item 4 (CHALK): core and dust #FBF3EC (was #FFFDF7 / #FFF7EC) at .92 on the top surface and .82 on the vertical front face; 7 px, taper, grain skips and dust bloom kept (_build/chalk.py). The lamp is now a FULL-strength overlay of #F09C28 (core 1 / .80 at .34 / .15 at .64, centred room (60, 560)) under an elliptical screen of rose-ivory #FFC0B0 55 % (room (20, 500), 300 x 220), low beside the cushion so the light falls away under the turn. Re-check once the halo fix lands; nothing in p04 touches the kandil. (SUPERSEDED by fix pass 3, item 3: the lamp is retuned; the numbers here are fix pass 2's.)

AI-10 is a shared plate (assets/ai/v3), and a re-cut means a new AI plate, the seam re-registered at x 540, the chalk, the C-HALO mask and the cuff's contact shadows re-measured, for a change the director marked as not needed for a pass.

THE BORDER'S TIMING: 6.00-7.15 s (brief: 1.0 s from 6.0).
